name: Front Hubs & Bearings
description: Non-driven front corners use a sealed, bolt-on hub bearing unit (Gen 3 style) with pressed wheel studs and an integral magnetic ABS encoder, bolted to the front knuckle from the inboard side.

components.name: Front wheel bearing & hub assembly
components.description: Sealed double-row angular-contact bearing unit with hub flange and five M14x1.5 studs. Slicks and big brakes load these bearings far beyond street use – treat as a consumable and check play every event.
components.location: Front knuckle bore, each side; flange outboard at z≈±0.72–0.76.

factory.name: GM front wheel bearing and hub assembly (Gen 6 Camaro, RWD)
factory.notes: Alpha-platform front hub units use 3x M12x1.75 knuckle bolts (Timken ATS listing – verify count on Camaro).

raceOptions.name: New OEM GM/ACDelco or Timken/SKF unit each season
raceOptions.notes: Most Gen 6 racers stay with OE-type sealed units and replace on a schedule.

raceOptions.name: Race hub with serviceable tapered bearings / larger studs
raceOptions.brand: Custom (e.g. for Trans Am style builds)
raceOptions.notes: Only if moving to center-lock or larger studs.

hardware.item: Front wheel bearing and hub assembly bolt
hardware.spec: M12x1.75 flange bolt (count/size per Alpha listing – verify)
hardware.torqueSequence: Clean the old threadlocker off the threads and apply new threadlocker. Torque all bolts in a cross pattern to 100 N·m (74 ft-lb), then turn each a further 15–30°.
hardware.threadlocker: Clean threads; re-apply threadlocker per SKF/OE (verify GM spec)
hardware.reuse: Replace (GM typically specifies new hub bolts)
hardware.notes: From GM 2016–18 table via TightTorque ("First pass"). [2026-10 check] The final angle is now filled in. The SKF 2023 Torque Specification Guide gives 2016–21 Camaro front hub mount at 74 ft-lb (100 N·m) with footnote [32] (+15° to 30°) and footnote [45] (new threadlocker). A camaro6.com owner quoting the SI for a 2018 ZL1 1LE gives 74 lb-ft + 15–30°, and TightTorque gives 100 N·m first pass. Note that the threadlocker field says 'none', but SKF says to re-apply threadlocker.

installNotes: Clean the knuckle bore and mating face; lightly coat the pilot with anti-seize to ease future removal.
Fit backing plate/dust shield first if it is clamped behind the hub.
Torque bolts in a cross pattern to the first-pass value, then apply the GM final angle.
Connect the wheel speed sensor and verify signal before closing up.
inspection: With the car on stands, rock the tire at 12/6 o'clock: any perceptible play = replace.
Spin and listen for roughness after each event.
Check rotor runout (bad bearings cause pad knock-back and long pedal).
